decision: Activate the bounded source-lock completeness audit. It is the highest-value feasible local recovery because the completed child-panic regression reached a reproducible materialization boundary before any semantic observation, and this static audit can determine the full local scope of that boundary without changing a frozen input or contacting an external source. Pipeline completeness remains the broader discovery alternative, but it remains blocked on its independent checked-object receipt-semantics protocol gate.

categories.assessment: The selected audit supplies a finite source-materialization method that closes a known local uncertainty without confusing it with acceptance behavior. Pipeline completeness remains a broader but protocol-unready discovery method.

The child-panic item left a precise missing-source boundary rather than a checker result. The audit creates a reusable, hash-bound ledger of every direct compile-time include edge visible in the pinned source tree.

The selected work is entirely local and makes no upstream claim or external request. Pipeline completeness also has no current external action, but cannot be promoted until its local scientific gate is resolved.

The audit reuses only the frozen source lock, pinned crate evidence and preserved build receipt; it neither fetches nor substitutes a source byte. Pipeline completeness needs a separately bound producer, adapter and receipt semantics before reuse is justified.

The selected audit directly characterizes the blocker exposed by the actual R2 build, while preserving the frozen source materialization and R2 evidence unchanged. Pipeline completeness is blocked locally by its required finite protocol, not by the source-lock audit.

candidates.rationale: ACTIVE under an exact committed entry package. Its one static parser scans only the 22 locked local Rust sources and records literal include paths against the same frozen inventory; it has zero build, checker, network, retrieval, substitution, mutation or external-action authority.

This remains the stronger broader conformance alternative, but no finite producer, adapter, checked-object receipt semantics, independently expected contents or fault rubric has been bound for execution.

blockers.reason: Bind the supported producer and adapters, a twelve-declaration expectation, receipt semantics, fixed faults and finite source/setup/build/tooling/process controls before promotion.
